subject: Intermittent inference failures impacting Polaris Health — incident update
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent inference failures impacting Polaris Health — incident update

Hi Michael / Polaris Ops team,

We observed a spike in failed or delayed /v1/generate requests affecting a subset of your tenant traffic starting ~2026-11-24 07:45 PST. You may have seen intermittent 5xx and elongated p95s for conversational requests. Our on-call engineers identified elevated queueing in the multi-tenant prefetch/batching layer that caused requests to be dropped or retried.

What were doing now:
- Shifted traffic away from the affected pool to a hot spare dedicated capacity for Polaris — this reduced error rate and latency for most requests.
- Temporarily reduced batch size and disabled speculative prefetching for your route to avoid further evictions.
- Increased ingest-side rate smoothing for a 30-minute window while we monitor.

Status and ETA:
- Mitigation is in place as of 08:02 PST; customers should see meaningful improvement within minutes.
- We will follow up with a full incident summary and a postmortem within 48 hours.

Workarounds you can apply on your side (if helpful):
- Pin the route to model variant redwood-lite for latency-sensitive calls until we finish root cause analysis.
- Reduce client-side concurrency/auto-retry windows for bursty traffic for the next 2 hours.

Link to current status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-24-prefetch-queue-surge

Im the primary contact for this incident; Ill keep you updated every hour or sooner for material changes. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts critical workflows.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Intermittent inference failures impacting Polaris Health — incident update

Hi Michael,

Short answers up front:
- We do not believe data was permanently lost; there were transient session resets for a subset of long-running conversations while requests retried. We are preserving full request/response traces for the affected window and will provide an excerpt (attached) for your team to correlate.
- Mitigation: the traffic shift to dedicated capacity has dropped error rate from ~6.7% to ~0.4% and p95 latency is trending back to baseline. We expect the next 2 hours to be stable while we validate.

Attached: polaris_ops_log_excerpt.txt (excerpt of request ids, timestamps, and error codes for 07:40-08:05 PST).

Were making a formal postmortem page and will host a 60-minute run-through tomorrow (Nov 25) at 10:00 PST to review root cause and long-term mitigations. Ill send a calendar invite — would that time work for you? If you prefer an earlier sync, we can do 08:30 PST as well.

For urgent needs, you can reach me or our on-call (Ben) at +1 (415) 555-0192.

Thanks for flagging this quickly.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: suspected prefetch/batch eviction regression — Polaris impact

Ben — pinging you to confirm what we observed: the telemetry shows a sudden increase in prefetch queue length and host-side eviction events correlated with a recent scheduler tweak deployed 11/24 07:30 PST. We rolled back that change in the affected pool, but I want eng to validate whether the change increased memory pressure leading to KV cache churn.

Immediate asks:
- Can you validate whether the scheduler patch increased per-worker memory footprint and whether any retry logic incorrectly amplified bursts?
- If confirmed, prepare an immediate rollback to the previous scheduling logic across other pools to prevent recurrence.

Jordan — Ill join the postmortem tomorrow and bring the raw telemetry dashboards.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>, Michael Chu <michael.chu@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Service restored — summary and next steps (Polaris Health)

Hi Michael / Polaris Ops,

Quick update — as of 12:40 PST we observed sustained restoration of your traffic to baseline error rates and latency. Summary of actions since my earlier note: 
- Rolled back the 07:30 scheduler tweak in the affected pool.
- Shifted your traffic to a hot spare dedicated pool and reduced batch size / speculative prefetching for your routes.
- Enabled additional monitoring alerts and increased log retention for the affected time window.

Impact assessment:
- Affected window: ~07:40-08:05 PST.
- Visible client impact: intermittent 5xx (primarily 504/502) and a small number of session restarts for long-running conversations.
- Data integrity: we have no evidence of permanent loss; we captured request/response traces for full forensics.

Next steps / deliverables:
- Complete root cause analysis and postmortem doc in our shared Drive by 48 hours: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/PM-INC-4321
- 60-minute postmortem review meeting scheduled: Nov 25, 10:00 PST (invite sent). Please let me know if you need a different time.
- A follow-up action plan will include regression detection for scheduler changes, automated canary throttles on prefetch toggles, and a recommendation to add a dedicated pool for sustained high-concurrency routes.

Attachment: polaris_ops_log_excerpt.txt (small excerpt to help correlate request ids).

Thanks again for your patience — well share the postmortem and prioritized remediation items shortly.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
